_note: Daily info bite for the audio brief: one short, fun line read right after "Good morning, Waynesville! It's <day>." Picked by scripts/day-bite.mjs in this order: (1) holidays computed by rule (Thanksgiving, Easter, Mother's Day, Memorial Day, Labor Day, clock changes and so on, coded in day-bite.mjs); (2) a fixed-date entry below, by MM-DD; (3) a countdown (Christmas from the day after Thanksgiving, Thanksgiving in the week before); (4) on Mondays, today's sunrise, sunset and hours of daylight in Waynesville; (5) on other days, a line from "pool" below, rotating one per day so no line repeats until the pool has gone round. A pool entry is a sentence, or {"text": ..., "months": [1-12]} to use it only in those months. Pool lines must be true and evergreen, never date-specific; don't start them with "It's". A countdown is added after (1) or (2) when one is running. Each fixed entry is a sentence written for the ear; keep it under about 120 characters, light and true. Add entries freely; a date can hold a list, and the line is then picked by year so it changes year to year.

fixed.01-01: Happy New Year! Here's to a great year in the village.
fixed.01-04: It's National Trivia Day, so here's one: Waynesville was laid out in 1797, before Ohio was even a state.
fixed.01-19: It's National Popcorn Day. Movie night, anyone?
fixed.01-21: It's Squirrel Appreciation Day, so give a nod to the busiest neighbors on your block.
fixed.01-23: It's National Pie Day. No judgment if that means pie for breakfast.
fixed.02-02: It's Groundhog Day. Whatever the groundhog says, spring officially arrives in about six and a half weeks.
fixed.02-09: It's National Pizza Day, a fine excuse to order from one of our local spots tonight.
fixed.02-14: Happy Valentine's Day! Downtown Waynesville makes for a pretty sweet date night.
fixed.02-29: It's Leap Day, the bonus day that comes around only once every four years.
fixed.03-01: Happy birthday, Ohio! Our state joined the union on this day in 1803, the seventeenth state.
fixed.03-14: It's Pi Day. Celebrate with a slice of pie, three point one four of them if you're ambitious.
fixed.03-17: Happy St. Patrick's Day! Wear a little green today.
fixed.04-01: It's April Fools' Day, so read everything twice today. Except this brief. This brief is real.
fixed.04-22: It's Earth Day, a good day for a walk on the Little Miami Scenic Trail.
fixed.05-04: It's Star Wars Day. May the Fourth be with you.
fixed.06-14: It's Flag Day. Look for the stars and stripes along Main Street.
fixed.06-19: Today is Juneteenth, the federal holiday marking the end of slavery in the United States.
fixed.07-04: Happy Independence Day! Have a safe and happy Fourth.
fixed.08-26: It's National Dog Day. Give your pup an extra treat today.
fixed.09-11: Today is Patriot Day, a day to remember the lives lost on September 11, 2001.
fixed.09-17: It's Constitution Day, marking the signing of the U.S. Constitution in 1787.
fixed.09-19: It's Talk Like a Pirate Day. Ahoy, Waynesville!
fixed.09-29: It's National Coffee Day. Treat yourself to a cup from a local shop.
fixed.10-31: Happy Halloween! Drive slowly tonight and watch for trick-or-treaters.
fixed.11-11: Today is Veterans Day. Thank you to every veteran in our community for your service.
fixed.11-13: It's World Kindness Day. Hold a door, pay a compliment, check on a neighbor.
fixed.12-04: It's National Cookie Day. You know what to do.
fixed.12-07: Today is National Pearl Harbor Remembrance Day, honoring those lost on December 7, 1941.
fixed.12-21: We're right around the shortest days of the year. From here on, the days start getting longer.
fixed.12-24: It's Christmas Eve. Wherever you're celebrating tonight, merry Christmas from all of us.
fixed.12-31: It's New Year's Eve. Have a safe and happy night, and see you next year.

pool: Waynesville is named for General "Mad" Anthony Wayne, the Revolutionary War hero.
Samuel Heighway, an engineer from Shropshire, England, laid out Waynesville in 1797.
Quaker families began arriving in Waynesville in 1801. The Museum at the Friends Home tells their story.
The first Ohio Sauerkraut Festival, in 1970, drew about 1,500 people, who ate 528 pounds of sauerkraut.
The Sauerkraut Festival began as a merchants' sidewalk sale, with a sauerkraut dinner added to draw a crowd.
Waynesville calls itself the Antiques Capital of the Midwest, and Main Street makes the case.
Caesar Creek Lake, a few miles east of the village, covers about 2,830 acres.
Fossil hunters can search the Caesar Creek spillway with a free permit from the visitor center.
Got a question about something happening in town? Email the editor with Ask the Brief in the subject line.
Know of an event we're missing? Send it our way and we'll add it to the calendar.
Every event on our calendar has an add-to-calendar button. Find it at waynesville dot news slash events.
Our Resources page puts local emergency numbers, crisis lines and county services in one place.
Looking for a plumber, a groomer or a good lunch? Our business directory lists more than 200 local businesses.
If you're looking to get involved, our Community page lists local clubs, youth sports and volunteer groups.
Shop local when you can. Every dollar spent in town helps keep Main Street going.
Check on an older neighbor today. A quick hello goes a long way.
Your library card at the Mary L. Cook Public Library opens up books, movies and more, all free.
Thanks for starting your day with us. If you like the Daily Brief, tell a friend.
Every source in today's brief is linked in the written edition at waynesville dot news.
You can get the Daily Brief in your inbox each morning. Sign up at waynesville dot news.
Grab your coffee. Here's what's happening around the village.
Whatever today brings, we hope it's a good one, Waynesville.
A little kindness goes a long way. Hold a door for someone today.
Don't forget to drink some water today. Your future self will thank you.
Spotted something new downtown? Let us know, and we might feature it.
News tip, event or correction? Reach us at editor at waynesville dot news.
If we ever get something wrong, tell us. We fix it and note the correction on the site.
Have a great day, and give a local business some love if you can.
Every brief comes in an audio version too. You're listening to it right now.
If you pass a neighbor this morning, give a wave.
Drive safe today, and watch for walkers and cyclists on the back roads.

pool.text: Good day for a ride or a walk on the Little Miami Scenic Trail, which runs right through Corwin.
Heading to Caesar Creek? Bring sunscreen and plenty of water.
School's out, so keep an eye out for kids on bikes around the neighborhoods.
Fall is a fine time to catch the colors along the Little Miami River.
Spring storms can pop up fast. Weather alerts on your phone are worth turning on.
With darker mornings, wear something bright if you're walking or running near the road.
Bundle up if you're heading out early, and give the windshield a few extra minutes.
Our Holiday Lights guide lists light displays near Waynesville, with dates, hours and prices.
